text: We think of the late night diner this way. A diner is set up to work 24/7 and keep open late into the night. That's either because night shift people need to come in, students, travelers, everybody. They have coffee, they have burgers, they have eggs. They have the staples. They have pie. They will last for a very long time. These are quick, easy meals that they can make at any time. So they have predictable costs. They also have overlapping shifts for their cooks and their waiters so that the grill stays hot, the coffee stays on. When it's 10, 11pm, you have the families that just came out of dinner and are going to hang out. 1am, you have taxi drivers. 5am, 6am, you have early morning commuters. But the diner is always kept warm, comfortable, inviting, so that people can come and sit and hang out for hours. And the cashier and the waiters will be very tolerant of people coming in alone and people coming in groups, sitting there for an hour, two hours. They don't rush people. And that's very important. And they are a comfort to people that have nowhere to go. That's what diners are about.
